items.headline: Winter Camp: Sign Up Now
items.body: Elite FC Winter Camp runs Dec. 27–31, 9:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., and it's open to all levels: footwork, technical and tactical drills, and games. Dec. 27 starts with a swag giveaway. K2 Fitness runs strength and conditioning on Dec. 28 and 30. On Dec. 29, a professional instructor leads yoga and breath control for competition, and lunch is served. Crepes on Dec. 31 celebrate the end of camp and 2026. Call it a tune-up for the second half of the season, or a good excuse to escape visiting relatives for a few hours. If you're going, let the club know as soon as possible for a headcount; contact the club for price and sign-up.

items.headline: Milinkovic Earns His A at Ultimate Cup
items.body:
Maksim Milinkovic finished fifth of 83 in Cadet Men's Epee at the Ultimate Cup in Hillsborough Township, N.J., on Oct. 31, and the result earned him an A rating, the highest USA Fencing awards. He had been a B since May.

The two-day regional at Iron Peak Sports & Events drew Elite FC fencers to Junior and Cadet events on both days. On Sunday, Nico Ng placed 10th in Junior Men's Epee.

Milinkovic is having a busy fall. Two weeks ago he was sixth at the FIE Cadet World Cup in San José, Costa Rica. His new rating reads A26: the letter, plus the year it was earned.

Next up for the club is the Cobra Challenge in Secaucus, Nov. 27–29, where 16 Elite FC fencers are entered.

items.headline: Photo from History: 1996 — Two golds at the start of an Olympic era
items.body: Laura Flessel won the first Olympic women’s individual epee title in Atlanta in 1996, then added team gold with France. The individual final was an all-French contest: she defeated Valérie Barlois 15–12. Born in Guadeloupe, Flessel began fencing at seven and became known as “The Wasp.” Her career stretched across five Olympics, with individual bronze in Sydney in 2000, individual silver and team bronze in Athens in 2004, and appearances in Beijing and London. She also won individual world titles in 1998 and 1999. This portrait was taken at the team trophy presentation of the 2013 Challenge international de Saint-Maur, a women’s epee World Cup event.
items.caption: Women’s epee made its Olympic debut in Atlanta in 1996, and Laura Flessel won both available gold medals for France: individual and team. This later portrait shows her at a women’s epee World Cup trophy presentation in Saint-Maur in 2013.

items.headline: Can the FIE tell you where not to fence?
items.body:
*The debate this fall on r/Fencing:* the world federation's warning about the new World Fencing League set off a 50-comment argument.

**What the FIE actually said.** According to the South China Morning Post, a statement signed by FIE Secretary General Gulnora Saidova on Oct. 22 said the league is not an official competition, and none of its planned events is sanctioned. It pointed to rules that allow bans. (We couldn't find the full text posted publicly.) The rule, Article 1.2.6(b), bars federation members from events run by anyone "not recognised by the national federation of their country," unless that federation specially authorizes them.

**What the WFL is.** It's a made-for-TV team league started by U.S. Olympian Miles Chamley-Watson. Its one event so far, in Los Angeles in April, offered a $100,000 prize pool. In épée, a 45-second clock punishes passive fencing.

**Opinion: it's overreach.** Running your own championships is fine, but banning members from someone else's show isn't. And "event" is never defined.

**Opinion: you signed up for it.** Joining a federation means accepting its rules. The FIE is worried about rivals, not club tournaments.

**What it means for club fencers.** By the rule's own wording, USA Fencing tournaments and events run by recognized clubs are unaffected. One wrinkle: USA Fencing itself signed a partnership with the WFL in January, and it hasn't commented publicly.

*Fact check:* Seven weeks before the warning, the FIE hosted Chamley-Watson in Lausanne for "positive discussions."

items.headline: By the Book: The 40-Millisecond Double
items.summary: Pitch: why both lights go on in épée. A double touch scores for both (t.92), and the box calls it a double only if the hits land within 1/25 to 1/20 of a second (40–50 ms, scoring-apparatus specs). It ties into the WFL's '40ms' rule in the Reddit box. About 70 words, written by Clark from the Oct 2026 USA Fencing rulebook.

items.headline: For the Parents: What a Rating Letter Means
items.summary: Pitch: a plain-words guide to USA Fencing ratings (A through E, U for unrated), what the year means (A26 = earned in 2026), how a fencer earns one (finish high enough at a big enough, strong enough event), and how long it lasts. Ties into Maksim's A26. About 110 words, sourced from USA Fencing's rules and Athlete Handbook.
